symptom: After `alter microflow … insert after $X begin if … end if; end` spliced a decision in, re-running the original `create or modify` (mdl 1) was refused — 'cannot drop the ExclusiveSplit … only an activity or a loop can be, because a decision or an end event changes the shape of the flow' — and so were `alter … drop '<caption>'` and `alter … replace '<caption>' with …`, so the script that created the flow could not be re-run
cause: The mutator's Drop/Replace went through removable(), which accepts an activity or a loop only: a decision is several nodes (split, path activities, merge) and the splice had no notion of taking a subgraph out; the statement diff already produced the right Drop/Replace op for the stored `if`
file: mdl/backend/mfmutator/splice_decision.go (insertedDecision, dropDecision, replaceDecision, pathNotes, DecisionNodes); mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (takenOut: path activities' outputs judged like the target's)
fix: Drop/Replace of a split validate it has exactly the shape `alter … insert` produces — two paths of plain activities (or none), each entered only by its predecessor, no error handler, rejoining at one merge entered by those two paths alone and leading on to one node — then rewire the split's incoming flows to the merge's successor (drop) or the fragment (replace) and take out the split, path activities, merge and the flows between them; notes attached only to path nodes go too. The shape check is the one verdict exec and check -p share (both run the mutator), and every out-of-shape decision is refused with the part that is out of reach ('its true path ends in a return', '… holds a decision', '… has an error handler', '3 flows join at its merge', 'it has 3 paths')
insight: No executor diff change was needed: the LCS already emitted Drop of the stored `if` (and Replace for a run starting at it), so the whole refusal lived in one mutator guard — check the verb the diff emits before designing a new op. Two traps for tests: the path activities' outputs must be judged like the target's (a variable a path declares and the flow reads after the merge), or the drop leaves a dangling reader; and a 'rebuild re-mints every $ID' control does not work inside one executor session — a flow dropped and created again there gets its stored identities back — so the churn control is a replaced activity (1 gone, 1 added)
